title: F₂ₘ = Fₘ·Lₘ: Factoring the Even-Index Difference of Squares via Lucas Numbers
description: Follow-up to the parent's even-index identity fib(2n+2) = fib(n+2)² − fib(n)². A difference of two squares always factors: a²−b² = (a−b)(a+b). Here a−b = fib(n+2)−fib(n) = fib(n+1) and a+b = fib(n+2)+fib(n) = L(n+1), the Lucas number. So the parent's difference of squares is the classical doubling product F₂ₘ = Fₘ·Lₘ. Mathlib has Nat.fib but no Lucas sequence, so this entry defines it, proves the Fibonacci–Lucas bridge L(n+1) = F(n) + F(n+2), and packages the doubling identity. Fully verified, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The Lucas numbers L = 2, 1, 3, 4, 7, 11, … satisfy the same recurrence as the Fibonacci numbers but start L₀ = 2, L₁ = 1. Édouard Lucas (1878) studied them alongside the Fibonacci sequence, and the pair satisfies a web of identities, the most fundamental being the doubling formula F₂ₘ = Fₘ·Lₘ. The parent gallery entry (FibonacciIdentitiesOQ03) established that even-index Fibonacci numbers are a difference of two squares, fib(2n+2) = fib(n+2)² − fib(n)². Since a difference of squares always factors, this entry asks what the factors are — and finds the Fibonacci–Lucas doubling product. Mathlib has Nat.fib but no Lucas sequence, so the entry also supplies that definition and the basic Fibonacci–Lucas bridge.
overview.problemStatement: **Follow-up to fibonacci-identities-oq-03**: the parent shows fib(2n+2) = fib(n+2)² − fib(n)². Factor this difference of two squares. Identify the factors fib(n+2) − fib(n) and fib(n+2) + fib(n), and express the result as the classical doubling identity F₂ₘ = Fₘ·Lₘ.
overview.text: A 107-line, fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file. It defines the Lucas sequence, proves the bridge L(n+1) = fib(n) + fib(n+2), the doubling identity fib(2m) = fib(m)·lucas(m), and the explicit factorization of the parent's difference of squares.
overview.proofStrategy: lucas_succ_eq_fib proves the Fibonacci–Lucas bridge L(n+1) = fib(n) + fib(n+2) by Nat.twoStepInduction: the base cases L₁ = 1 = fib₀ + fib₂ and L₂ = 3 = fib₁ + fib₃ are decidable, and the step expands L(n+3) = L(n+1) + L(n+2), applies the two inductive hypotheses, and collapses all Fibonacci terms with fib_add_two before ring. fib_two_mul_eq then proves fib(2m) = fib(m)·lucas(m): the m = 0 case is trivial, and for m = n+1 it rewrites fib(2n+2) via Mathlib's product form fib_two_mul_add_two and the Lucas bridge, closing by ring (since fib(n) + fib(n+2) = 2·fib(n) + fib(n+1)). fib_even_factorization specializes the doubling identity to expose the parent's difference of squares as the literal product fib(n+1)·(fib(n+2)+fib(n)).
keyInsights: A difference of two squares always factors, so the parent's fib(2n+2) = fib(n+2)² − fib(n)² must be a product — and the factors are the Fibonacci number fib(n+1) and the Lucas number L(n+1).
fib(n+2) − fib(n) = fib(n+1) is just the Fibonacci recurrence; fib(n+2) + fib(n) = L(n+1) is the Fibonacci–Lucas bridge.
The result is the fundamental doubling identity F₂ₘ = Fₘ·Lₘ, here proved for all m (the m = 0 case fib 0 = 0 included).
Lucas numbers are new to this gallery and to Mathlib; the entry contributes the definition and the basic bridge L(n+1) = fib(n) + fib(n+2) alongside the headline identity.

conclusion.summary: The even-index difference of two squares from the parent entry, fib(2n+2) = fib(n+2)² − fib(n)², factors as the Fibonacci–Lucas doubling product fib(n+1)·L(n+1), i.e. the classical identity F₂ₘ = Fₘ·Lₘ. The entry introduces the Lucas sequence (absent from Mathlib) and the bridge L(n+1) = fib(n) + fib(n+2).
conclusion.implications: Identifying the factors of the parent's difference of squares connects two standard Fibonacci facts (the sum-of-squares and difference-of-squares doublings) through the Lucas numbers, and provides reusable Lucas infrastructure for future gallery work (e.g. L²−5F² = ±4, L₂ₘ, and divisibility identities).
